heard: Scientists turned planet Earth into one giant radio dish. Eight observatories targeted a galaxy 55 million light years away. Every dish synchronized its recordings using atomic clocks. But the raw data was way too massive for the internet. Engineers had to fly petabytes of hard drives on airplanes. Supercomputers processed the data into humanity's first black hole image. The shadow spans nearly 40 billion kilometers across. Its ring of light could swallow our entire solar system. No single telescope on Earth was big enough.
